text:
katie: Heads up — onboarding orion-lite-14b v2 (int4) to prod tests. Seeing intermittent OOMs and a lot of memory fragmentation on 4xA100 nodes when traffic spikes. Also noticed a small quality dip on long-form summarization prompts after quant.
ryan: Can you paste the minimal repro? rough batch sizes and max_new_tokens you used?
katie: Repro path: POST /v1/generate model=orion-lite-14b-v2- int4, batch_size=8, max_new_tokens=512. Failing ~1/200 requests on our stressbench. OOM log: "CUDA out of memory when allocating 256 MiB" followed by KV cache compaction messages.
nash: (typo) ash: I ran a local canary with batch_size=4 and max_new_tokens=256 — no OOMs in 10k requests. Throughput dropped ~12% but stable.
nora: Do we have perf diffs vs fp16/int8? any quality numbers for int4?
katie: Quick bench: fp16 baseline: 135 req/s, int4 current: 158 req/s but with 0.9% failure rate under burst. int4-quality on summarization (ROUGE-L): fp16 0.72, int4 0.69 (small but consistent).
ryan: Two-prong plan: 1) mitigate OOMs by changing defaults + deployment knobs (reduce default max_new_tokens to 256, soft cap per-request; soften microbatching to prefer latency), 2) dig into quant calibration for those attention-heavy layers.
nash ash: For (1) try config: ```
model_defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  batch_size_soft_limit: 6
  prefetch_kv: true
  kv_eviction_threshold: 0.6
  slab_align: true
```
katie: Will roll that to a canary. Also propose adding a slot compaction debug flag to collect fragmentation histograms.
ml-oncall-bot: Incident note: canary rollout will be monitored; alert on OOM rate > 0.1% or latency p95 > 2s.
nora: For quant quality: run per-layer range analysis and try outlier-folding for the FFN layers. Also compare symmetric vs asymmetric clipping. I can run a 5k-sample eval if you push the quant artifacts.
ryan: If per-layer folding helps, we can keep int4 for cost, but temporarily enable fallback-to-int8 on high-attention seqs (seq_len>1024) — implement as a routing rule.
katie: Canary schedule: push defaults + frag-hist logging at 14:00 UTC, run 2h smoke, then widen to 10% traffic. I'll attach logs to this thread.
nash ash: One more note — observed that enabling slab_align reduced fragmentation by ~18% in my local stress harness. Worth keeping.
nora: I'll queue the quant eval and post results. If we see ROUGE drop >0.02, we should gate and try per-layer or mixed-precision fallback.
katie: Thanks — next actions: (1) ryan to add routing fallback rule, (2) ops to push model_defaults change to canary, (3) nora to run eval, (4) collect frag histograms and heap dumps if OOM happens.
ryan: On it. I'll also add a temporary metric for "kv_compact_count" so we can correlate compactions to failures.
ml-oncall-bot: Note recorded: playbook steps for model-onboard frag/OOMs linked: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/model-frag-oom
katie: OK rolling now. Will update when canary completes. :thumbsup:
